metrics.name: QA Score
metrics.note: Typical industry benchmark for ticket quality is 90-95%.

metrics.name: SLA Attainment
metrics.note: % of tickets resolved within the committed SLA window, per issue category.

metrics.name: Attendance / Adherence
metrics.note: Directly tied to the reported attendance / hours-not-met issue driving current gaps.

metrics.name: CSAT
metrics.note: Post-interaction satisfaction survey. Ecommerce/retail benchmark typically 85-92%.

metrics.name: AHT (Average Handle Time)
metrics.note: 8-min goal / 10-min cap. Balanced against QA, not optimized in isolation.

metrics.name: First Response Time (Tickets)
metrics.note: 4h goal / 6h cap. Reasonable standard for email/chat tickets in ecommerce.

metrics.name: Backlog Health (% tickets ≤ 2 days)
metrics.note: Core metric for the central problem: aged, unresolved tickets.

metrics.name: Sentiment Score
metrics.note: % of resolved interactions tagged positive/neutral. Protects brand reputation.

metrics.name: Brand Voice / Tone QA
metrics.note: Qualitative scorecard check: empathy, on-brand tone, public-facing risk management.

metrics.name: First Response Time (Social)
metrics.note: 15-min goal / 30-min cap. 73% of social media users switch brands if response is slow.

metrics.name: Resolution Time (Social)
metrics.note: 4h goal / 8h cap from first contact to full thread resolution.

metrics.name: Volume / Productivity
metrics.note: Comments + DMs resolved per agent per shift, across FB/IG/TikTok.

metrics.name: Escalation Rate
metrics.note: % of interactions requiring escalation to Tier 2 or another department.

story: Kitsch started in 2010 with the everyday basics — hair ties, clips, the small things we reach for again and again. The original business plan was barely a paragraph long.

Since then, Kitsch has grown from door-to-door hair-tie sales into a beauty brand carried in over 20,000 retail locations across 27 countries — while staying true to the same idea: create beauty essentials that are a step above, made as sustainably as possible, and priced so they're within everyone's reach.

Kitsch is female-founded and female-owned, built on the belief that consistency and hard work compound into something real. The brand calls the small daily pauses for self-care — fixing your hair, taking a breath before the next thing — "Kitsch Moments": little resets that give people a boost to keep going.
founderBio: Cassandra Thurswell started Kitsch at 25, working out of her LA apartment — cold-calling stores and selling hair ties door-to-door before building her own line.
She bootstrapped the business and grew it gradually over more than a decade, staying close to what everyday customers actually wanted rather than chasing trends.

Today Kitsch products sit on shelves at Ulta, Sephora, and Whole Foods, and Cassandra has been recognized by outlets like Forbes and Inc. — but the philosophy hasn't changed: stay useful, stay accessible, stay close to the community.
culture.mission: To create accessible, elevated beauty essentials — for hair and for everyday self-care — made as sustainably as possible, so our community always feels a little more ready for whatever the day brings.
culture.vision: To be the brand people reach for first — not because we're everywhere, but because we understand them: their hair, their hustle, and their need for a little boost along the way.

values.name: Community First
values.description: We stay close to the people we serve. Every product, every conversation, starts with actually listening.

values.name: Elevated Simplicity
values.description: We take the everyday things people reach for again and again, and make them a little better — better quality, better design, better for the planet.

values.name: Sustainability with Purpose
values.description: From ocean plastic recovery to clean water access, we make choices that matter beyond the shelf — not just a checkbox.

values.name: Positivity & Grit
values.description: We started with a one-paragraph business plan and door-to-door sales. Showing up, staying positive, and doing the work is how you build something real.

values.name: Accessible Indulgence
values.description: Self-care shouldn't be a luxury. We create small moments of care that are within everyone's reach, for every hair type, every budget.

kitschMomentsInCX.intro: Kitsch defines a "Kitsch Moment" as any small pause in someone's day that gives them a little boost — a reset, a transition, a bit of self-care. In Customer Experience, every ticket, comment, or DM is a Kitsch Moment waiting to happen. Our job isn't just to close the case. It's to leave that person feeling a little more taken care of than before they reached out. That takes two things from every one of us: staying emotionally grounded even in a hard interaction, and leading with honesty and follow-through so people can always trust what we tell them.

behaviors.title: Reset
behaviors.description: When a customer is frustrated, we stay grounded and de-escalate before we jump to a solution — their emotion isn't a personal attack, it's a signal.

behaviors.title: Reassure
behaviors.description: We confirm, in plain language, that the person was heard — before we start solving.

behaviors.title: Delight
behaviors.description: When there's room, we add a small human touch that shows we see a person, not a ticket number.

behaviors.title: Follow Through
behaviors.description: We tell people the truth, even when it's not what they want to hear — and a Kitsch Moment isn't complete until they know exactly what happens next.

givingBack.intro: Sustainability at Kitsch isn't a side project — it's part of how the brand operates.

items.title: 4ocean Partnership
items.description: Every shampoo or conditioner bar sold funds the removal of the ocean-plastic equivalent of one bottle from oceans, rivers, and coastlines.

items.title: Charity: Water
items.description: Kitsch committed $10,000 to build a community well in Uganda, providing clean water access to 300+ community members.

items.title: Vegan & Cruelty-Free
items.description: Products are made with animal-friendly materials — never derived from or tested on animals.

items.title: Recycled & Reusable
items.description: From packaging to hair elastics, Kitsch favors recycled materials and reusable alternatives over single-use.

leadershipPhilosophy.title: How We Lead
leadershipPhilosophy.intro: Leadership at Kitsch shows up the same way our products do: practical, consistent, and genuinely caring. Every coaching conversation, every 1:1, and every piece of feedback in this tool is built on two simple ideas — stay grounded, and lead with integrity.

pillars.name: Stay Grounded
pillars.description: The strength to stay calm and clear-headed during a hard interaction, a hard month, or a hard conversation — without losing empathy for the customer or the team.
practices: Leaders regulate their own state before coaching a tough moment.
A frustrated customer is a signal to solve for, not a personal attack.
Sustainable pace and self-care are treated as part of performance, not separate from it.

pillars.name: Lead With Integrity
pillars.description: Leading — and serving customers — through consistency, honesty, and follow-through, not authority.
practices: We tell people the truth, even when it's not what they want to hear.
1:1 coaching is built on transparency: clear metrics, clear expectations, clear next steps.
Every interaction is a chance to leave someone a little better than we found them.

rollout.name: Diagnose
rollout.description: Scorecard runs in observation-only mode. Real Actuals are collected for every metric to build a true root-cause map, but weights are not yet used to evaluate performance formally.

rollout.name: Structure
rollout.description: Weights and goals are formalized and communicated to the team. The scorecard runs in shadow/pilot mode (50% operational weight) alongside the new escalation matrix, SOP library and attendance policy.

rollout.name: Scale & Accountability
rollout.description: KPI governance is fully live (100% weight), tied to a formal coaching cadence, tier classification, and the peak-season staffing playbook.
